5| """Define constants for keys.
6| 
7| Each key constant is defined as a Key object, which allows comparison with
8| strings (e.g. 'A', 'Escape', 'Shift'). This enables handling of key events
9| without using the key constants explicitly (e.g. ``if ev.key == 'Left':``).
10| 
11| In addition, key objects that represent characters can be matched to
12| the integer ordinal (e.g. 32 for space, 65 for A). This behavior is mainly
13| intended as a compatibility measure.
14| 
15| """

18| class Key(object):
19|     """Represent the identity of a certain key.
20| 
21|     This represents one or more names that the key in question is known by.
22| 
23|     A Key object can be compared to one of its string names (case
24|     insensitive), to the integer ordinal of the key (only for keys that
25|     represent characters), and to another Key instance.
26|     """

29|         self._names = names
30|         self._names_upper = tuple([v.upper() for v in names])
